title: POC weekly sync - quantization INT8/FP8 results review
summary: Weekly sync to review INT8 and FP8 quantization experiment results, discuss quality deltas, latency/cost tradeoffs, and agree next steps for benchmark runs and acceptance criteria. Redwood outlined recent kernel changes and fallback strategy; Nimbus asked for additional fidelity checks and 2-week extended eval on production prompts.
topics: INT8 vs FP8 quality delta summary
End-to-end latency and token throughput deltas
Per-batch cost impact and autoscale behavior
Regression detection and eval set expansion
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-19 10:00 PDT
Duration: ~45m
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Liam (Nimbus), Maya (Nimbus), Sofia (Nimbus)

Summary (auto): Quick recap of last week's baseline, went through INT8 and FP8 numbers, talked about a few outlier prompts where FP8 lost coherence, discussed perf deltas on A100 + H100 testbed and Dedicated config, agreed on running longer production-like run and share updated benchmark sheet.

[00:00] Alex: hey everyone, thanks for joining, can you all hear me ok?
[00:04] Liam: yep good here, thanks alex.
[00:07] Priya: morning! we'll jump straight in — short agenda, results then open discussion.
[00:15] Alex: quick reminder, notebook link and benchmark sheet are in the doc — shared: https://redwood.sheets/quant-bench (shared).
[00:28] Maya: saw that, thanks. baseline was run on h100 right? the dedicated nodes?
[00:33] Priya: yes baseline and INT8/FP8 both ran on our dedicated test cluster — H100s for FP8 and A100 for INT8 microbench, we noted kernel improvements last week that changed per-token latency a bit.
[00:48] Sofia: quick question on datasets — are you using the production prompt set or the cleaned eval set?
[00:52] Priya: both — primary is our prod-like prompt set (2.5k samples) plus the curated eval (500 prompts) to catch regressions.
[01:10] Liam: ok going to the numbers — I see FP8 reduces memory by ~38% and avg latency down 12% but the quality drop on the NLI and summarization tasks is concerning, hit about 1.8% BLEU-ish delta on short prompts? (laughs)
[01:26] Priya: yeah that was one of the surprising bits — for summarization FP8 lost some factual anchors on the longer context, INT8 was closer to baseline in most cases. There are a handful of outlier prompts where FP8 hallucinated a date or name.
[01:45] Alex: do you remember which prompts? can we mark them as the "regression set" and run per-token logprobs?
[01:51] Sofia: we flagged ~12 examples, I'll add them to the sheet — some are multi-step instructions which seem more sensitive.
[02:10] Maya: on perf — the throughput lift for FP8 at batch=8 was solid, but we saw tail latency increase slightly on warmup for very short requests. kind of odd.
[02:21] Priya: noted, the warmup is likely kv cache behavior plus the new fused kernel path; we'll dig into the trace.
[02:30] Alex: side note: we did an A/B where FP8 fell back to INT8 on detected regressions; that reduced the overall quality delta but added ~6% cost. worth discussing.
[02:46] Liam: interesting, fallback seems reasonable if it's automated. what's the detection threshold?
[02:52] Priya: current heuristic is drop in confidence/logprob beyond X and a simple ngram overlap check; it's experimental. we can make it stricter for your production run.
[03:10] Sofia: can we do a heads-up run that sends diffs on any generated tokens flagged? maybe webhook into our QA?
[03:16] Alex: yes we can push diff hooks to your QA, we used that in another POC. will need an endpoint from you.
[03:25] Maya: also need SLO discussion — if we route some traffic to Dedicated and some to Hosted fallback, how do we guarantee latency?
[03:33] Priya: autoscale + reserved slots on Dedicated will keep p50 tight; p95 we saw increase for mixed routing but we can limit burst routing to keep p95 under your SLA.
[03:45] Liam: about cost — sheet shows FP8 improved tokens/sec and cost/unit but fallback reduces savings; can you show end-to-end cost with 5% fallback rate?
[03:55] Priya: yes we have a cost model tab, I'll update with a dynamic fallback scenario.
[04:10] Alex: quickly on security/compliance — you asked for KMS integration and audit logs last time, we're still collecting those artifacts and will share SOC2 and KMS integration doc this week.
[04:20] Maya: perfect, also SSO SAML stuff for the console.
[04:24] Alex: yup will share the SSO guide.
[04:30] -- (brief screen share of benchmark sheet) --
[06:00] Priya: we also ran a latency breakdown per op: attention kernels improved for FP8 on H100, but softmax stability required a different casting path. that's likely causing some small generation artifacts.
[06:30] Sofia: that matches where we saw dropped facts — seems like numerical stability. any mitigation short-term?
[06:38] Priya: we can enable mixed-cast softmax fallback for those layers — it slightly increases memory but helps factuality. we'll test toggles.
[07:00] Liam: ok run plan? what do we agree to run next week for acceptance?
[07:06] Alex: propose: 1) 72-hour production-like run at 10k requests/day with live-shaped prompts; 2) expanded regression set (Sofia to add flagged prompts); 3) perf+trace capture for warmup tails (Priya to instrument); 4) automated diff webhooks to Nimbus QA.
[07:25] Maya: 72 hours sounds good, we want to see stability across load spikes.
[07:30] Sofia: I'll upload the flagged prompts by EOD tomorrow.
[07:34] Liam: we also need a clear pass/fail — i'd say <1% quality delta on your primary metric and p95 under 450ms on Dedicated.
[07:44] Priya: noted — we'll aim for that and diagram fallback thresholds.
[10:00] Alex: quick recap and next steps — we'll share updated benchmark sheet, priya will run the 72-hour test starting Monday, Sofia to push regression prompts, alex to send SOC2/KMS/SSO docs, and we'll reconvene next Tuesday same time.
[10:20] Maya: thanks everyone, sounds good.
[10:25] Liam: thanks all.
[10:30] (call ends)

Alex to share SOC2, KMS, and SSO/SAML docs by 2026-05-21
